documents.title: Academic Integrity (Writing Center)
documents.stance_why: The page does not ban AI; it says "unattributed AI use" is academic misconduct and offers help with using AI "ethically", implying attributed use is acceptable, so permit with an attribution condition.
documents.summary: Writing Center page on academic integrity. Its single AI rule lists unattributed AI use as academic misconduct, and it points students to the Office of Community Standards and Compliance with questions.

units.why: The sentence frames the Writing Center as a "supportive, judgment-free space" for ethical use of "new tools like AI". It is a service statement, not a rule, and fits no type (P10 tells students to ask the instructor), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Writing Center consultants provide a supportive, judgment-free space to help you understand plagiarism
units.uncovered_note: Writing Center offers consultations to help students understand plagiarism, citation and ethical AI use; a student-support service with no rule.

units.why: Lists "unattributed AI use" among forms of "academic misconduct", so AI use without attribution is misconduct. Fits P36 (classified as misconduct); P24 does not fit because the sentence classifies rather than instructs disclosure. Attributed use is implicitly tolerated, hence restrict.
units.anchor: academic misconduct, which also includes cheating, fabrication, unauthorized collaboration, unattributed AI use, and more

units.why: Says that if unsure about attribution "or how to use AI tools ethically", students should reach out to the Office of Community Standards and Compliance. This is ask-before-acting guidance, so P10.
units.anchor: unsure about when attribution is needed—or how to use AI tools ethically
units.frag_end: what happens if a violation is reported.

documents.unit: Center for Faculty Excellence (AI Faculty Learning Community), Teaching and Learning at CSU pressbook
documents.title: Example Policy Statements for AI in Higher Education
documents.stance_why: The page says there is likely no "one size fits all policy" and statements "will be determined by individual instructors, departments, and programs", then gives sample syllabus statements ranging from required acknowledgment to open permission.
documents.summary: Faculty Learning Community page collecting sample syllabus statements from six CSU instructors, plus links to other universities. It sets no institutional rule; statements range from required acknowledgment to open permission.

units.why: States that there is likely no "one size fits all policy" and statements "will be determined by individual instructors, departments, and programs", so the decision is delegated: P04.
units.anchor: AI policy statements will be determined by individual instructors, departments, and programs.

units.why: Hughes-Lynch: "you are required to acknowledge use of AI in any work you submit", a disclosure duty with each submission: P24, must; unit_stance permit since use is allowed with acknowledgment.
units.anchor: you are required to acknowledge use of AI in any work you submit for class
units.frag_start: Because it can also be abused,

units.why: Hughes-Lynch: copied AI text "must be treated as any other direct quote and properly cited", an attribution rule. P24 chosen over P45 because the focus is citing, though a quote analogy is used.
units.anchor: must be treated as any other direct quote and properly cited

units.why: Hughes-Lynch: "Other uses of AI must be clearly described at the end of your assignment", a separate disclosure-of-other-uses rule: P24.
units.anchor: Other uses of AI must be clearly described at the end of your assignment.

units.why: Koc: "Do not rely solely on AI tools to complete assignments" and use AI "as a supplement rather than a replacement", so students stay the primary thinker: P32.
units.anchor: using AI tools as a supplement rather than a replacement for your own work

units.why: Koc: "Do not use AI tools to plagiarize"; using AI to generate or modify content to evade detection "violates academic integrity", so it is classed as misconduct: P36.
units.anchor: to evade plagiarism detection is unethical and violates academic integrity

units.why: Koc: "Do not assume that AI responses are always correct" and AI can "generate fake results", a verification warning: P31.
units.anchor: Do not assume that AI responses are always correct.

units.why: Liu: "Use of AI tools, including ChatGPT, is permitted in this course", a default permission: P02.
units.anchor: Use of AI tools, including ChatGPT, is permitted in this course.

units.why: Liu: students are "only encouraged to use AI tools to help brainstorm assignments or projects", an encouraged brainstorming use: P15 (not P02 because it names a specific use).
units.anchor: you are only encouraged to use AI tools to help brainstorm assignments or projects
units.policy: Students are only encouraged to use AI tools to help brainstorm assignments or projects.

units.why: Liu: students are encouraged to use AI "to revise existing work you have written", a writing-support use: P18, separate from brainstorming.
units.anchor: or to revise existing work you have written
units.policy: Students are encouraged to use AI tools to revise existing work they have written.

units.why: Liu: "It is sorely your responsibility to make all submitted work your own", an ownership rule: P29.
units.anchor: It is sorely your responsibility to make all submitted work your own

units.why: Liu: AI content "may not meet the standards of this course, even if you only incorporate such content partially", a warning about quality and accuracy: P31.
units.anchor: quality of AI generated content may not meet the standards of this course

units.why: Liu: AI content "may not provide appropriate or clear attribution" to original authors while assignments need APA-guided scholarly sources; a verification warning about attribution: P31 (not P52, since it concerns sources, not licensing).
units.anchor: AI generated content may not provide appropriate or clear attribution
units.frag_end: latest publication manual of the APA.

units.why: Liu: instructor "reserve[s] the right to use various plagiarism checking tools ... including those screening for AI-generated content, and impose consequences accordingly", use of detection tools: P40.
units.anchor: plagiarism checking tools in evaluating your work, including those screening for AI-generated content
units.frag_start: Lastly, as your instructor, I reserve

units.why: Rauschert: "If you are ever unsure about whether collaboration with others, including using artificial intelligence, is allowed or not, please ask me right away", ask-first rule: P10.
units.anchor: unsure about whether collaboration with others, including using artificial intelligence, is allowed

units.why: Rauschert: for labs students may "try using AI" but "must all create your own code, output and answers", so AI cannot produce submitted work: P19.
units.anchor: you must all create your own code, output and answers

units.why: Rauschert: "Quizzes will be done in class and must be solely your own work", an in-class assessment rule: P22 (AI is not named in this sentence but the passage is about AI collaboration).
units.anchor: Quizzes will be done in class and must be solely your own work.

units.why: Rauschert: "You alone are always responsible for the correctness of the final answers", an ownership rule: P29.
units.anchor: You alone are always responsible for the correctness of the final answers

units.why: Rose: AI tools "are not prohibited in the course. In fact, we will explore their uses", permitted and used in the course: P02.
units.anchor: Artificial Intelligence tools like ChatGPT and other copilots are not prohibited in the course.

units.why: Rose: "required to submit original work (that is not generated by AI) for all assessments", so AI may not produce submissions: P19.
units.anchor: required to submit original work (that is not generated by AI) for all assessments

units.why: Rose: the original-work rule "means citing if you use AI-generated text and how you apply it", a disclosure duty: P24.
units.anchor: citing if you use AI-generated text and how you apply it in your work

units.why: Rose: LLMs "have been known to supply inaccurate information and fake citations", so students should corroborate AI information: P31.
units.anchor: Use your information literacy skills to corroborate AI information

units.why: Rose: "Failure to cite your use of AI or using fabricated information could result in your violation of the Academic Honesty Policy", nondisclosure is the violation: P28 (not P36, which covers misuse generally).
units.anchor: Failure to cite your use of AI or using fabricated information could result in

units.why: Schell-Barber: ChatGPT use "is neither encouraged nor prohibited", so it is allowed by default: P02 (permit).
units.anchor: use of Chat GTP is neither encouraged nor prohibited from use on assignments

units.why: Schell-Barber: ChatGPT "should not be used as a way to produce first and only drafts", a limit on AI-produced work: P19.
units.anchor: should not be used as a way to produce first and only drafts
units.frag_start: Chat GPT is simply a tool

units.why: Schell-Barber: "Chat GPT is quickly becoming a communication tool in most business settings", a professional-practice justification: P44.
units.anchor: Chat GPT is quickly becoming a communication tool in most business settings.

units.why: Schell-Barber: "It is your responsibility to review and revise all work before submitting", an ownership rule: P29.
units.anchor: It is your responsibility to review and revise all work before submitting

units.why: Schell-Barber: "Chat GPT may not develop high-quality work that earns a passing grade", a quality warning: P31.
units.anchor: Be aware that Chat GPT may not develop high-quality work that earns a passing grade.

notes: Coder B. No university-wide AI policy found; the Writing Center page and the exemplar syllabus statements are the only sources. Neither document is computing-specific.
